aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: four high-confidence agents favor it, including interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and concept accuracy, all with very strong confidence around 0.96-0.99. These dimensions indicate Lesson 1 teaches the math coherently, has a functioning quiz interaction, and aligns narration and visuals reasonably well. Lesson 2 wins visual accuracy and polish, with moderate-to-high confidence, because its slides are cleaner and more visually consistent, while Lesson 1 has rendering and layout glitches. However, Lesson 2's severe narration problems, lack of interactivity, missing timing data, and pedagogical incoherence outweigh its visual advantages.
